replicated_originals.reference: Simpson, Vondrová & Žalská (2018) Sources of shifts in pre-service teachers' patterns of attention: the roles of teaching experience and of observational experience

A.reason: Cited as [24] (Sherin & van Es, JTE 60(1), 2009; online 2008, so the year variant is benign) as a seminal video-club study and an example of increased interpretation; the paper's design and replication comparison are anchored on Simpson et al. (2018), not on this practising-teacher video club study.

B.reason: The intervention 'was designed to closely mirror the approach in' [25], used its coding manual and individual-level analysis, and the discussion treats the study as a divergent replication of Simpson et al. (2018), noting its similar sample and design, after failing to reproduce the shift in pre-service teachers' attention.

notes: Self-described 'divergent replication' (title); the authors say it was not designed as a replication but should be considered one. The finding tested (video interventions shift pre-service teachers' professional vision toward students, subject matter and specifics, away from evaluation) is attributed to Simpson et al. (2018) and, more loosely, to the Sherin/van Es literature it builds on. A second coder might also count van Es & Sherin (2010) or Sherin & van Es (2009) as originals, but the paper names Simpson et al. (2018) as the design it closely followed. Star et al. (2011)/Star & Strickland (2008) appear only as an example of an earlier replication in the field.
